questions.q: How do you estimate the money needed to become financially independent?
a: Divide your yearly expenses by four
Save four times your annual salary
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to multiply annual expenses by 25, which works because of the 4% withdrawal rule.

questions.q: How much of their income does the FIRE approach suggest saving and investing?
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the aim is to put away and invest roughly half to most of what you earn.

questions.q: Which kind of stock investment does the summary recommend?
questions.why: Lesson 2 says index funds are cheap and match the market average, and that Warren Buffett prefers them.

questions.q: What does the summary say about income and the FIRE method?
a: It can work at any income, depending on what you do with it
It requires a six-figure salary to get started
It only works for people without children
It depends more on income than on spending habits
questions.why: Lesson 3 says what you earn matters less than what you do with the money, citing a couple earning under $50,000.

questions.q: What is the core of the FIRE mentality?
a: Maximizing earnings at any personal cost
Never spending money on travel or fun
Retiring as young as physically possible
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the mindset is less about extreme saving and more about valuing happiness over possessions.
